name: flrh-agent-runtime-boundary
purpose: Evaluate whether deterministic functional, logic, reactive, harness, and typed-graph mechanics justify a reusable agent runtime boundary.
rationale: No executable runtime or production consumer exists yet.
Durability, recovery, effect reconciliation, and graph interoperability are specified but unmeasured.
The smallest justified next step is a mechanics vertical slice rather than a broad engine framework.

boundary.owns: Deterministic transition, fixpoint, signed-delta stabilization, and typed effect-intent output
boundary.mechanism: Compute a stable FLR transition from explicit snapshots, events, rule bundles, and dataflow profiles while H controls commit and effects
boundary.state_authority: A future fenced H store would own accepted state; the current repository owns specifications only

contract: evaluate(snapshot, accepted_event, rule_bundle, dataflow_profile) -> StableTransitionAndEffectIntents | TypedRejection
invariants: Identical explicit inputs and versions produce identical canonical output.
F, L, and R never execute external effects.
R never publishes a reaction batch before the logical frontier passes.
Unknown external outcomes require reconciliation before retry or terminal success.
failure_model: Malformed or incompatible inputs yield typed rejection without mutation.
Non-convergent logic or dataflow reaches a bounded pathology outcome.
Checkpoint or version incompatibility fails closed.
Evidence gaps prevent terminal success rather than being inferred away.
verification: Property tests compare replay and worklist-order invariance.
Incremental insert, delete, and retract results match clean full recomputation.
Crash injection covers intent commit, dispatch, external success, receipt, and reconciliation boundaries.
Resolved production and harness composition graphs differ only by approved adapter substitutions.
promotion_gates: At least two current consumers share the stable narrow-waist contract.
M0 through M5 mechanics admission gates pass with durable receipts.
A fenced single writer, recovery, cancellation, schema migration, and effect reconciliation are demonstrated operational requirements.
Policy variation remains outside the shared mechanism without core forks.
falsifiers: Real tasks repeatedly require ambient effects inside the deterministic kernel.
Incremental results fail to converge to clean recomputation.
Planned consumers require incompatible semantics rather than shared adapters.
The boundary adds more coordination and state than it removes.
